verdict.rationale: Dagster lets engineers declare asset dependencies in code (e.g., `@dg.asset(deps=[hello])`). Declarative Automation uses the status of assets and their dependencies to launch executions, and conditions such as `on_cron` run an asset only after all upstream dependencies have updated, which is dependency-ordered orchestration. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration that runs execute in correct dependency order at scale; the community evidence only praises the asset-centric approach in general terms.

support.subject: As a data engineer, I define dependencies between pipeline steps and datasets, and the platform orchestrates runs in the right order

citations.quote: Declarative Automation is a framework that uses information about the status of your assets and their dependencies to launch executions of your assets.
The AutomationCondition.on_cron will execute an asset once per cron schedule tick, after all upstream dependencies have updated.
Dagster then helps you run your functions at the right time and keep your assets up-to-date.
making it easy to chain an Airbyte sync with upstream or downstream steps in your workflow.
